design.title: Probe first, then fine-tune, actually trained: one extra opening epoch trains only the head on the FROZEN ImageNet trunk before the usual fine-tune (LP-FT; re-run of experiment 21, which never reached a GPU)
design.init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for 1 epoch, then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
design.eli5: The model's 'eyes' were borrowed from a network that had already looked at a million everyday photos, and that borrowed vision is what lets it recognise Berlin in a photograph it has never seen. Until now we started teaching the eyes and the brand-new 'map-reading' part at the same moment - so in the first hours the confused new part was yanking the borrowed eyes around. Now the map-reading part first practises for one round with the eyes held still, and only then are both tuned together, so the eyes keep more of what made them useful. (This idea was planned once before, but the rented computer could not be reached, so it was never actually tried.)
design.hypothesis: Experiment 21's hypothesis was never tested. Its run died before training on an infrastructure error: train_berlin.log ends in botocore EndpointConnectionError ('Could not connect to the endpoint URL: https://ec2.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/'), so the scorer recorded 1e9 and the harness marked it REVERTED. That verdict says nothing about LP-FT, exactly as experiment 17's crash said nothing about ring pooling (re-run as 18) and experiment 24's said nothing about Noisy Student weights (re-run as 25); issue #13 has since stopped cloud failures passing as refuted ideas. The champion is still experiment 20 (0.0777: truedop_2024 usable 93.0%, false 0.75% = 3 frames, abstain 6.25% = 25 frames; the three training photographs 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints), and model/ is identical to the code experiment 21 branched from, so its reasoning stands unchanged. The reasoning: every large step on the never-seen photograph this era came from what the pretrained trunk brought with it (exp 12 MobileNetV3-Small 10.75% -> 49.5% usable; exp 16 MobileNetV2 86.75%; exp 19 EfficientNet-B0 92.5%), and exp 20 showed that HOW the trunk is trained still moves the held-out number (a better point on the same trajectory: +0.5 usable, false 1.0% -> 0.75%). Today the trunk is fine-tuned from step 1 jointly with a randomly initialised head (prototypes std 0.01 over 2,970 tiles, random lifts, random embed BatchNorm), so the earliest, largest gradients into the pretrained blocks come from a head that knows no tile yet, and the trunk BatchNorm statistics start drifting at the same moment. Kumar et al. (ICLR 2022, 'Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution') show that full fine-tuning from a random head distorts pretrained features along in-domain directions and costs out-of-distribution accuracy while in-domain accuracy is unchanged; training the head on the frozen trunk first (LP-FT) removes most of that loss. That is our split precisely: in-domain saturated at 100%, held-out survey at 93%. It also answers the plateau the right way: the last three trained experiments (22 continuous vantages, 23 cross-survey consistency loss, 25 Noisy Student init) changed sampling, loss and init and none moved the held-out number beyond noise; the one stage never questioned since exp 12 is the trunk's fine-tuning procedure ('0.1x LR from step 1'). Exp 25 is mild evidence against a pure 'better init' story, which makes the complementary question - does the fine-tune PRESERVE whatever the init brings - the informative next test. Builds on experiment 20 (champion) and lifts experiment 21's never-run implementation verbatim.
